title: How Intuit uses LLMs to explain taxes to millions of taxpayers - Jaspreet Singh, Intuit

summary: Jaspreet Singh details Intuit's GenAI architecture for TurboTax, which processed 44 million tax returns for tax year 2023. The platform, called GenOS, includes genux (UI layer), an orchestrator with a planner for routing queries to different LLM solutions, and powers 'Intuit Assist.' The team distinguishes between static queries (explanations of known tax outcomes like refund summaries) and dynamic queries (user questions such as product help or tax-situation questions like 'can I deduct my grandchild's tuition'). Claude serves static explanations; OpenAI GPT-4 mini handles dynamic Q&A. RAG and GraphRAG incorporate IRS form changes and Intuit's proprietary tax engines, with GraphRAG outperforming regular RAG and personalized answers outperforming even GraphRAG for end-user helpfulness. A fine-tuned Claude 3 Haiku via AWS Bedrock was piloted for static queries—quality improved with fewer instructions and smaller prompts, reducing latency, but the model became too specialized. Evaluation is phased: tax analysts provide manual evaluations and serve as prompt engineers during development, creating a golden dataset (using AWS Ground Truth) that feeds automated LLM-as-judge evaluations (using GPT-4 series) for ongoing iteration. Major changes like tax-year transitions trigger manual re-evaluation. Critically, LLMs never perform tax calculations—all numbers come from Intuit's proprietary tax knowledge engine, and ML-based safety guardrails detect hallucinated numbers before responses reach users. Tax experts specifically craft and test prompts for each static explanation scenario, ensuring legal and privacy compliance. The team is constantly evaluating new models including in-house ones, but has not yet decided on models for the next tax year.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: Intuit processed 44 million tax returns for tax year 2023, requiring GenAI explanations at massive scale.
GenOS is Intuit's proprietary generative OS platform, built because off-the-shelf tooling didn't meet regulatory safety and scale requirements.
Static tax explanations use Claude; dynamic user Q&A uses OpenAI GPT-4 mini, with GraphRAG outperforming regular RAG and personalized answers outperforming both.
LLMs never perform tax calculations—all numbers come from Intuit's proprietary tax knowledge engine, with ML guardrails detecting hallucinated numbers.

Phased evaluation starts with tax expert manual reviews and prompt engineering, then transitions to automated LLM-as-judge (GPT-4 series) scoring; major changes like tax-year transitions trigger manual re-evaluation.
A query planner routes incoming questions to different solutions based on question type (product help vs. tax situation).
Vendor lock-in is significant—contracts, prompts, and even same-vendor model upgrades are costly and non-trivial.
LLM latency (3–10 seconds) balloons with complex user tax situations, requiring fallback mechanisms and careful product design.

sections.title: Introduction and Scale
sections.summary: Jaspreet Singh introduces himself and Intuit's goal of helping TurboTax users understand taxes, noting 44 million tax returns processed for tax year 2023.

sections.title: TurboTax Experience and GenOS Platform
sections.summary: Describes the TurboTax explanation experience and GenOS, Intuit's proprietary generative OS platform built for regulatory safety and scale, including genux (UI), orchestrator, and Intuit Assist.

sections.title: LLM Architecture: Static and Dynamic Queries
sections.summary: Details the system architecture: Claude for static prepared-statement queries, OpenAI GPT-4 mini for dynamic user Q&A, RAG and GraphRAG for tax knowledge, and a fine-tuned Claude 3 Haiku pilot that was too specialized.

sections.title: Evaluation Pillars and Tax Expert Integration
sections.summary: Covers key pillars including human domain experts (tax analysts) who serve as prompt engineers, phased evaluation from manual to automated, LLM-as-judge, and migration from Claude Instant to Claude Haiku for tax year 2024.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning Claude 3 Haiku and Data Compliance
sections.summary: Describes fine-tuning Claude 3 Haiku via AWS Bedrock to reduce prompt size and latency, with compliance to IRS 7216 regulations using only consented user data.

sections.title: Evaluation Details and Automated Tooling
sections.summary: Expands on automated evaluation pillars (accuracy, relevancy, coherence), LLM-as-judge operating on golden datasets from AWS Ground Truth, and in-house automated prompt chaining tooling.

sections.title: Major Learnings: Vendor Lock-in, Latency, Evals
sections.summary: Key learnings: expensive vendor lock-in via contracts and prompts, latency challenges (3–10 seconds) requiring fallback design, and the absolute necessity of evaluations and golden datasets before launch.

sections.title: Q&A on Evaluation Timing
sections.summary: Discusses LLM-as-judge using GPT-4 series for expensive evaluations, with minor iterations handled by auto eval and major changes like tax-year transitions triggering manual re-evaluation.

sections.title: Q&A: User Question Types and Query Planner
sections.summary: Explains that users ask both product questions (how to do something in TurboTax) and tax situation questions (e.g., deducting grandchild's tuition). A query planner routes incoming questions to different solutions based on type.

sections.title: Q&A: Number Verification and Hallucination Prevention
sections.summary: Clarifies that LLMs never perform tax calculations—all numbers come from Intuit's proprietary tax knowledge engine. ML-based safety guardrails detect hallucinated numbers in raw LLM responses before they reach users.

sections.title: Q&A: GraphRAG vs RAG, Personalization, and Future Models
sections.summary: GraphRAG outperforms regular RAG for response quality, but personalized answers outperform even GraphRAG for end-user helpfulness. The team is constantly evaluating new models including in-house ones and Claude 4, but has not decided on next tax year's models.

sections.title: Q&A: Answer Generation and Legal Compliance
sections.summary: Explains that static query answers use numbers from the tax knowledge engine with tax-expert-crafted prompts tested for each scenario. Intuit focuses heavily on legal and privacy controls to prevent wrong answers.
